title.en: Flat and solid shapes, kinds of lines and symmetry

text.en: The biscuits fit together in the box so well because they are all rectangular and the same size.

Observe the faces of a matchbox, a book and a biscuit box. What is common? They are all rectangular.
A square has four equal sides. A rectangle has two long sides and two short sides.
Draw the outline of a cuboid and you may get a rectangle, or a square if two sides are equal.
Name three objects with rectangular faces, like a book, a door and a tile.
Flat shapes like triangle, circle, square and rectangle are drawn on paper. Solid shapes can be held.
Straight lines and curved lines make these shapes. A circle is made of one curved line.
(additional, not in the textbook) If you can fold a shape so that both halves match, it has a line of symmetry. A square folded from corner to corner matches.
